market.summary: A strong academic-union opportunity with broad Thai/local-language coverage, alongside substantial national and municipal public libraries. Major university catalogs are heterogeneous and migrating: WALAI AutoLib and ALIST are locally developed families; Innovative, Koha and Alma/Primo also occur. Public university discovery does not establish general-public lending.
market.platform_strategy: Prioritize a dedicated UC-TAL/WALAI union adapter for institution-listed holdings, then investigate permissioned direct circulation adapters. ALIST merits a second family prototype; current PSU React/API frontend differs from older ASP.NET routes. Do not deploy automatic Primo scraping across disallowed search paths. Existing Koha adapter is only a separate candidate at allowed local installations.

adoption_evidence.claim: 1 August 2015 institutional survey lists ALIST 27 adopters, WALAI AutoLib 68, LM-SomSook 2. Historical scoped counts, not current national market shares.
adoption_evidence.scope: Historical 2015 Thai higher-education-supported LMS account, not national census

limitations: No national largest-ten ranking established; size dates, units and institutional proxies cannot be compared as ranks.
Ten selected institutional observations are based on three shared union queries, not ten independent endpoint tests.
Union named holding institutions and local record links were returned. No campus, exact shelf, copy count, refresh date or live circulation status established.
Primary catalog restrictions remain in force; separate UC-TAL observations do not grant permission to query restricted local endpoints.
Union deep links for Mahidol and Silpakorn visibly lag their newer platform/routes; a returned URL is not a verified working link.
Related-title works, a Cliff’s Notes guide, Thai translations and illustrated editions were preserved as separate identities; no cover ISBNs promoted to record ISBNs.
Empty Holding/GetHolding arrays for five books are not absence: returned institution mappings exist; that endpoint supplies serial-style holdings.
UC-TAL frontend robots is ordinary Angular fallback; API robots has explanatory comments only. Neither establishes reuse licence.
No patron authentication, outreach, hold requests, catalog harvesting, application edits or live app integration test.
Regional and municipal public libraries remain unverified; the feasible selected sample is academic and must not imply representative nationwide LMS market share.
